title: If the nightly backup is switched off, the outage alarm stays quiet for good
what: The 10-minute outage check treats a backup that answers "not set up" the same as "not switched on yet" and calls it fine. So if the backup store is ever unhooked or removed in a later change, no copy of the gym data is made each night and no alarm is raised, with no end date.
expected: Once the backup has been switched on, an answer of "not set up" counts as down and opens the outage note like a failed night does.
how_often: only if the backup is unhooked, then every night
fix_line: After the switch-on date, treat a "not set up" backup answer as down

title: The outage alarm never checks WhatsApp sign-in codes or the AI service
what: The 10-minute alarm only asks whether the websites, HQ, the gym server and the backup answer. Nothing scheduled checks that WhatsApp still delivers sign-in codes or that the AI service still answers; the WhatsApp check exists only as a hand-started run to the owner's own phone. If WhatsApp refuses MettleUp's number or template, members cannot sign in by phone and MettleUp hears about it from a gym.
expected: A timed check (or a count of failed sends) for WhatsApp code delivery and the AI service, raising the same outage note.
who: members signing in by phone, gyms using AI
fix_line: Add WhatsApp and AI health to the 10-minute check, from a failure count on the server

items.reason: The only live write here is the outage note on GitHub; each part is tried 3 times, a GitHub failure fails the run and the next run 10 minutes later tries again; that a broken run is quiet is already filed.
Runs never overlap (queued, not cancelled) and each run first looks for the open outage note, so a retry does not open a second note. No fault.
Supabase and Cloudflare sites are watched; WhatsApp and AI are not; payment companies already filed. Play outages affect only releases, which fail red.
Restore drill runs on test data on every push; a real night's copy was never restored (already filed); a switched-off backup reads as fine (new).
Only one timed job lives in this folder (the 10-minute watch); if it breaks it fails quietly (filed). The daily crash job lives in a private repo: not readable here.
Each DOWN line logs why, the key reminder failure logs its reason, and a crash of the watch logs the error. No fault in this folder.

The cloud tests cover rest in deep Doze, app killed mid-rest, exact alarms denied, and the watch workout with always-on on and off and wrist down. Heart rate off the wrist cannot run on an emulator: belongs to the watch area code read.
Rule applied: what the emulators cannot show here (a real wrist, a real screen-off sensor) is left to the watch and phone code areas; this folder holds only the tests.
Site, sign-in server and backup outages raise an emailed note within about 10-30 minutes; WhatsApp codes, AI, the every-minute alert job and a switched-off backup do not.

Job failure alerts: the outage note. Crash reports: a daily job in a private repo (not checked). Error reports: none (filed). No daily all-is-well line: a silent watch looks the same as a stopped one (filed).
No workflow collects sign-up, activation, day-30 or paid numbers; already filed for HQ.
